title: Read the list backwards
prompt:
Byte stacked the parts list upside down. The list `parts` is in the right order. Build a new list named `backwards` that holds the same parts in the opposite order.

Leave `parts` itself alone. When it works, `python3 backwards.py` prints the reversed list.
hints: Start with an empty list: `backwards = []`. Which item should go into it first?
A `for` loop gives you each part from the front. `insert(0, part)` puts a part at the very front of `backwards`.
Inside the loop write `backwards.insert(0, part)`. The slice `parts[::-1]` also works, if you like shortcuts.
explain_after:
Each `insert(0, part)` pushed the newer part to the front, so the first part ended up at the back. `insert` changes the list and returns `None` [py-074], which is why the line stands on its own.

Your original list stayed the same because you built a new list. A slice also returns a new list [py-077].
